name: Broadcom Inc.
monetization: Sells custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and AI networking silicon to hyperscalers and labs — OpenAI 10GW and Anthropic 3.5GW TPU deals — plus VMware infrastructure software.
description_md: Broadcom designs custom AI accelerators ('XPUs') co-developed with a small set of very large customers — Google's TPUs are the flagship program — alongside merchant AI networking (Tomahawk/Jericho switches, optical/PCIe interconnect) and a large infrastructure-software business (VMware). It is the principal beneficiary of hyperscalers and labs diversifying away from Nvidia GPUs into custom silicon; management cites six core custom-chip customers including Google, Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
ai_monetization_md: AI semiconductor revenue was $10.8B in Q2 FY2026 (+143% y/y), guided to $16.0B in Q3 (+200%+ y/y); the company has reiterated FY2026 AI revenue of ~$56B and an FY2027 target in excess of $100B. Economics are long-cycle co-development contracts: OpenAI committed to 10GW of Broadcom-co-designed accelerators (deploying 2026–2029), and Broadcom will supply Anthropic with ~3.5GW of Google-designed TPU capacity from 2027 under an April 2026 three-way deal that also extends Broadcom's TPU development agreement with Google to 2031. Contract dollar splits per customer are undisclosed — a known data gap.
ai_strategy_md: Be the arms-dealer for custom silicon: capture every hyperscaler/lab that wants an alternative to Nvidia by co-designing XPUs and bundling its networking stack (the 'open Ethernet vs NVLink' pitch). Concentrate on a handful of >$1B/yr customers rather than merchant volume; use VMware cash flows to fund the ramp. The FY27 >$100B AI target implies AI would roughly double again — predicated on OpenAI and Anthropic deployments landing on schedule.
risk_notes_md: **Customer concentration:** six custom-silicon customers drive the AI business; the two largest new commitments (OpenAI 10GW, Anthropic 3.5GW) are labs whose own funding is the ecosystem's central open question — Broadcom backlog sits in the committed-but-unfunded tier until deployments are financed. **Guidance risk:** the June 2026 selloff (unchanged FY26 AI forecast, soft VMware) showed the stock is priced for raises, not reiterations. **Disclosure:** per-customer ASIC contract values are not public; revenue mix is inferred by analysts.

events.title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce 10GW custom-accelerator collaboration
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI commits to co-developed Broadcom ASICs (racks deploying 2026–2029) — the largest custom-silicon program announced, and the backbone of Broadcom's FY27 >$100B AI target.

events.title: Anthropic signs for ~3.5GW of Google TPUs supplied via Broadcom from 2027
events.why_it_matters: Expands a 1GW 2026 arrangement; Broadcom simultaneously extended its Google TPU development deal to 2031. Anthropic disclosed run-rate revenue >$30B, framing the capacity as demand-backed.

events.title: Q2 FY26: AI revenue +143%, but shares drop on unchanged FY26 AI forecast
events.why_it_matters: Demonstrated how much AI growth is already priced in — a reiterated ~$56B AI guide plus soft VMware sales read as a miss.
